title: Fresh Popup-Clearance Canary Attempt Result
summary: A fresh FP-MCP-233 structured approval was recorded, committed, and validated. The new FP-MCP-232 popup-approved local clearance tool created a short-lived local clearance for the exact tuple without manual Python scripting. A guarded start request for FP-MCP-223 was then accepted by the remote runner. OpenCode started successfully with runnerRunId RUN-20260703T174527866Z-8630e8a1 and completed a DESIGN_ONLY run. Runner pre/post start evidence, stdout/stderr logs, and the produced DESIGN_ONLY outputs were committed under runs/FP-MCP-223/deepseek-v4-pro-high-DESIGN_ONLY/. Approval consumption recording was attempted after start, but the existing consumption recorder refused due an approval-scope/text contract mismatch; this remains a follow-up fix and no duplicate start was attempted.
caveats: Approval consumption evidence was not recorded because forgepilot_record_human_approval_consumption refused with APPROVAL_SCOPE_MISMATCH, APPROVAL_REQUEST_BINDING_INVALID, and APPROVAL_TEXT_INVALID.
The failed approval-consumption recorder behavior appears to be a contract mismatch separate from the guarded start path.
The OpenCode run output claims DESIGN_ONLY boundary preserved, but the start itself necessarily contacted the runner start endpoint and started OpenCode as intended for this canary.
No second guarded start attempt was made after the successful start.
The popup-created local clearance expires and must not be reused.
